articles.summary: Leading national before- and after-school care provider supports families through partnerships with more than 1,150 schools across the country. Key takeaways For the 2026–27 school year, Champions is launching new partnerships with school districts including Cupertino Union School District (California), Decatur School District 61 (Illinois), Iowa City School District (Iowa), and Spotsylvania County Public Schools (Virginia), expanding access to high-quality afterschool programs for working families. Champions partners with elementary and middle schools to provide safe, supervised before- and after-school as well as school break programs. Champions works with state agencies, federal programs, employers, and schools to help eligible families access child care tuition assistance and other affordability resources. articles.summary: California, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Virginia all make strides toward increasing family access to high-quality early childhood education and care Key takeaways: KinderCare applauds California, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Virginia for prioritizing early childhood education and care in their latest budgets. KinderCare helps deliver publicly funded early learning programs through its programs in these states, making high-quality child care more accessible to working families. Each state’s investments in child care assistance and early learning programs will help thousands of children access high-quality education and care. KinderCare supports policies that increase child care affordability, strengthen workforce participation and expand access to high-quality early childhood education. articles.summary: First Arkansas location marks KinderCare’s 42nd state, bringing high-quality early childhood education and care to Arkansas families Key takeaways: KinderCare Learning Companies opened its first early childhood education center in Arkansas, bringing access to high-quality early childhood learning and care to families in Bentonville. Bentonville KinderCare serves children ages six weeks to five years old and provides a nurturing learning environment designed to help children build confidence, develop essential skills and prepare for kindergarten. The opening comes as Northwest Arkansas continues to grow, creating increased demand for reliable child care solutions that support working families and local employers. KinderCare Learning Companies, Inc.
